design_notes.note: Avoid routing any high-frequency signal close to an analog signal line: keep digital switching signals such as PWM or JTAG away from the oscillator circuit and from ADC signals. Keep the external crystal traces short with proper grounding to reduce parasitic capacitance.

Decouple DVCC/DVSS with a 10 uF plus 100 nF low-ESR ceramic pair placed within a few millimetres of the pins. TI additionally recommends separated analog and digital grounds joined at a single point, for noise isolation from digital-to-analog circuits on the board and for analog accuracy. The Recommended Operating Conditions make the bulk capacitor mandatory (CDVCC = 4.7 to 10 uF, +/-20% or better) because it is what limits the supply slew rate below the 0.2 V/us that would trip a BOR.

source.section: 7.1.1 Power Supply Decoupling and Bulk Capacitors

design_notes.note: ADC layout: ground loops form when ADC return current shares a path with other analog or digital circuitry, generating small offset voltages that add to the reference or input. Quickly switching digital signals and noisy supply lines corrupt conversion results, so the ADC input trace must be shielded from them. Putting the MCU into a low-power mode during the conversion improves ADC performance in a noisy environment.

This device supports only a low-frequency (32 kHz) crystal on XIN/XOUT, and external load capacitors for it are required. A digital clock may be applied to XIN instead in XT1BYPASS mode, freeing XOUT. Unused XIN/XOUT pins must be terminated per Section 4.6.
The VQFN thermal pad (pin 25, 2.7 x 2.7 mm) must be soldered to the PCB for thermal and mechanical performance.

DVCC must never exceed the Absolute Maximum limits during power-up, power-down or operation: exceeding them can cause erroneous writes to RAM and FRAM, i.e. silent data corruption rather than a clean failure. System-level ESD protection must be applied in compliance with the device-level ESD specification to prevent electrical overstress or disturbance of data or code memory.

provenance.notes: Both offered packages (RGE VQFN-24 4x4 mm and YQW DSBGA-24 2.29 x 2.34 mm) appear in theta_ja; mechanical records the VQFN. Package dimensions were read from the RGE0024H outline drawing on PDF page 89, which pdftotext cannot decode (the page uses an unsupported AutoCAD character collection), so the page was rendered to an image and the dimensions read from the drawing. The dissipation_model is marked 'assumed': TI publishes supply-current tables but never writes a dissipation formula for this part, so P = VCC x I_active is our composition of stated facts and must be reviewed as such. No radiated emissions: no transmitter. The two conducted-emissions entries are the device's clock domains, taken from the Recommended Operating Conditions ceilings rather than from any measured emission -- TI publishes no emission amplitude, di/dt or ripple for this part, so those fields are absent. Note the unusually low 85 C junction limit, which equals the maximum ambient: this part has effectively no thermal headroom above a hot board.
